# `core` command reference

The consumer CLI, shipped in `core-cli` (this page: version 1.0.2, the released package). Most commands talk to a running CORE API. See the [CLI overview](../cli-reference.md) for which binary does what.

42 commands.

| Group | Commands | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [`code`](#code) | 14 | Codebase quality, style, and verification operations. |
| [`lane`](#lane) | 4 | Assisted Remediation Lane: work delegated findings under human-gated approval. |
| [`project`](#project) | 4 | Operations for project lifecycle: onboarding and documentation. |
| [`proposals`](#proposals) | 6 | Operations for the A3 Autonomous Proposal system (propose, approve, execute). |
| [`secrets`](#secrets) | 5 | Manage encrypted secrets in the database. |
| [`symbols`](#symbols) | 4 | Operations for the symbol registry and Knowledge Graph identification. |
| [`vectors`](#vectors) | 5 | Vector store operations (Qdrant). |

## `core code` {#code}

Codebase quality, style, and verification operations.

### `core code actions` {#code-actions}

```
core code actions
```

List all registered Atomic Actions (Body Capabilities).
Shows IDs, categories, and impact levels for autonomous building blocks.

### `core code audit-duplicates` {#code-audit-duplicates}

```
core code audit-duplicates [OPTIONS]
```

Perform a semantic scan to find duplicate logic across the codebase.
Helps enforce the 'dry_by_design' constitutional principle.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--threshold` | `0.96` | Similarity threshold (0.0-1.0). |

### `core code baseline` {#code-baseline}

```
core code baseline [OPTIONS]
```

Create a secure checksum baseline of the current 'src/' directory.
Run this before starting autonomous tasks.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--label`, `-l` | `default` | Label for this baseline. |

### `core code bridges` {#code-bridges}

```
core code bridges [OPTIONS]
```

List declared architecture bridge points.

Each bridge is a constitutionally-declared data-flow crossing where
information moves between CORE layers. Use --consuming to find bridges
that consume a specific data type.

Example:
  core code bridges --consuming AuditFinding

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--consuming`, `-c` |  | Filter by consuming type (e.g. AuditFinding, Proposal). |

### `core code check-imports` {#code-check-imports}

```
core code check-imports
```

Verify all import statements resolve to existing modules.

Checks for:
- F821: References to undefined names (moved/deleted modules)
- F401: Stale imports left after refactoring

Enforces:
- code.imports.must_resolve
- code.imports.no_stale_namespace

### `core code check-ui` {#code-check-ui}

```
core code check-ui [OPTIONS]
```

Check and repair Body-layer UI contract violations.

Validates that logic in features/ and services/ does not use:
- print() or input()
- rich.console or formatting
- os.environ (must use shared.config.settings)

If --write is used, CORE invokes an AI specialist to refactor the
violating modules into a headless state.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` | off | Use LLM to autonomously fix UI contract violations. |

### `core code docstrings` {#code-docstrings}

```
core code docstrings [OPTIONS]
```

Autonomously generate and inject missing docstrings using AI.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` | off | Apply changes. |
| `--limit` | `3` | Symbols to process. |
| `--file` |  | Target a single file (repo-relative). |

## `core lane` {#lane}

Assisted Remediation Lane: work delegated findings under human-gated approval.

### `core lane claim` {#lane-claim}

```
core lane claim FINDING_ID [OPTIONS]
```

Mark a delegated finding as being worked, so it is tracked, not parked.

Claiming does not change the finding's status — it stays a live lane item —
it only records who is working it (ADR-109 §2).

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FINDING_ID` | required |  |
| `--agent`, `-a` | `claude-code` | Identity of the working agent. |

### `core lane list` {#lane-list}

```
core lane list [OPTIONS]
```

List delegated findings awaiting assisted remediation (indeterminate + human).

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--limit`, `-n` | `20` | Max delegated findings to show. |
| `--full-ids`, `-f` | off | Show full finding IDs instead of truncating. |

### `core lane next` {#lane-next}

```
core lane next
```

Show the oldest delegated finding (the FIFO head of the lane) with detail.

The agent's "pull next work" surface. The rich context bundle (related
files, guidance, rule text) is the deferred #653 exporter; for now this
surfaces the finding's own payload so you know what to work next.

### `core lane propose` {#lane-propose}

```
core lane propose FINDING_ID [OPTIONS]
```

Validate an agent-authored diff and, if it clears, submit it for approval.

Flow (ADR-109): read the finding's rule, run ``assisted.validate_diff``
against the diff in a throwaway worktree (apply + ruff + the offending rule
must no longer fire + mapped tests), and only on a clean verdict create the
human-gated proposal and move the finding out of the inbox into "being
worked". A diff that fails validation never reaches the approval queue.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FINDING_ID` | required |  |
| `--patch`, `-p` | required | Path to the unified diff the agent produced for this finding. |

## `core project` {#project}

Operations for project lifecycle: onboarding and documentation.

### `core project docs` {#project-docs}

```
core project docs [OPTIONS]
```

Generate the canonical Capability Reference documentation.

Extracts all public symbols and their intent from the database.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | `docs/10_CAPABILITY_REFERENCE.md` | Target path for the reference doc. |

### `core project onboard` {#project-onboard}

```
core project onboard PATH [OPTIONS]
```

Onboard an existing repository into CORE governance — Phase A (BYOR).

Delivers the machinery floor (META schemas, taxonomies, constitution stub,
enforcement/config) into the target's .intent/. No rules are included; run
`project scout` afterwards to induce and ratify rules for this repo (ADR-119).
Dry-run by default; pass --write to apply.

Pass --write --stage to write to work/staged/&lt;name>/ first, inspect the
files, then run `project onboard promote <path>` to deliver to the target.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | required |  |
| `--write` | off | Write .intent/ directory to the target path. |
| `--stage` | off | Write to work/staged/&lt;name>/ for inspection before promoting (ADR-123). Requires --write; ignored in dry-run mode. |

### `core project promote` {#project-promote}

```
core project promote PATH
```

Promote a staged machinery floor into the target repository (ADR-123).

Reads from work/staged/&lt;name>/.intent/ (within CORE's repo) and writes to
&lt;path>/.intent/. Run `project onboard promote --help` for full lifecycle details.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | required |  |

### `core project scout` {#project-scout}

```
core project scout PATH [OPTIONS]
```

Induce and ratify governance rules for a repository — Phase B (BYOR Scout).

Calls the CORE API to extract signals and propose candidate rules
(LLM-assisted; falls back to a universal menu when LLM is unavailable).
Walks you through per-rule ratification. Only confirmed rules are written
(ADR-119 D5 — no --accept-all). Requires Phase A first:
run `project onboard <target> --write` before this command.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PATH` | required |  |
| `--write` | off | Write inducted rules to .intent/ after ratification. |
| `--reset` | off | Clear existing scout_inducted.json and re-run induction. |

## `core proposals` {#proposals}

Operations for the A3 Autonomous Proposal system (propose, approve, execute).

### `core proposals approve` {#proposals-approve}

```
core proposals approve PROPOSAL_ID [OPTIONS]
```

Authorize a pending proposal for execution.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROPOSAL_ID` | required |  |
| `--by` | `cli_admin` | Approver identity. |
| `--authority` | `principal.governor` | Authority under which approval is granted (URS NFR.5). |

### `core proposals create` {#proposals-create}

```
core proposals create GOAL [OPTIONS]
```

Create a new autonomous proposal for system modification.

Validates the plan and performs an initial risk assessment.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GOAL` | required |  |
| `--action`, `-a` |  | Format: action_id:param=value |
| `--file`, `-f` |  | Specific files affected. |
| `--write` | off | Persist the proposal. Dry-run by default. |

### `core proposals execute` {#proposals-execute}

```
core proposals execute PROPOSAL_ID [OPTIONS]
```

Execute an approved proposal.

Runs the atomic action sequence defined in the proposal.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROPOSAL_ID` | required |  |
| `--write` | off | Apply changes to the system. |

### `core proposals list` {#proposals-list}

```
core proposals list [OPTIONS]
```

List recent autonomous proposals and their risk assessments.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--status`, `-s` |  | Filter by status (pending, approved, etc.) |
| `--limit`, `-n` | `20` | Max results. |
| `--full-ids`, `-f` | off | Show complete proposal IDs instead of truncating. |

### `core proposals reject` {#proposals-reject}

```
core proposals reject PROPOSAL_ID [OPTIONS]
```

Reject a proposal and prevent its execution.

Revival of deferred findings (ADR-010 §7a / ADR-045) now happens
on the API side; this command only renders the result.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROPOSAL_ID` | required |  |
| `--reason`, `-r` | required |  |

### `core proposals show` {#proposals-show}

```
core proposals show PROPOSAL_ID
```

Show detailed breakdown and risk assessment of a proposal.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROPOSAL_ID` | required |  |

## `core symbols` {#symbols}

Operations for the symbol registry and Knowledge Graph identification.

### `core symbols audit` {#symbols-audit}

```
core symbols audit
```

Audit symbol integrity: drift summary and unassigned ID report.

### `core symbols fix-ids` {#symbols-fix-ids}

```
core symbols fix-ids [OPTIONS]
```

Assign stable '# ID:' anchors to all untagged public symbols.

Scans 'src/' and modifies files to ensure knowledge graph stability.
Pass --write to apply changes (default is dry-run).

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` | off | Inject missing UUIDs into source files. |

### `core symbols resolve-duplicates` {#symbols-resolve-duplicates}

```
core symbols resolve-duplicates [OPTIONS]
```

Find and resolve duplicate '# ID:' anchors in the codebase.

The older entry is preserved; colliding symbols receive fresh identifiers.
Pass --write to apply changes (default is dry-run).

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` | off | Regenerate conflicting UUIDs. |

### `core symbols sync` {#symbols-sync}

```
core symbols sync [OPTIONS]
```

Synchronize filesystem symbols with the PostgreSQL Knowledge Graph.

Scans 'src/' and updates the 'core.symbols' table.
Pass --write to apply changes (default is dry-run).

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` | off | Apply synchronization to the database. |

## `core vectors` {#vectors}

Vector store operations (Qdrant).

### `core vectors query` {#vectors-query}

```
core vectors query QUERY [OPTIONS]
```

Semantic search in vector collections.

Search constitutional documents using natural language queries.

Examples:
    core-admin vectors query "file access rules"
    core-admin vectors query "atomic actions" --collection patterns --limit 3

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `QUERY` | required |  |
| `--collection`, `-c` | `policies` | Collection to query: 'policies', 'patterns', 'specs', or 'code' |
| `--limit`, `-n` | `5` | Max results to return |

### `core vectors rebuild` {#vectors-rebuild}

```
core vectors rebuild [OPTIONS]
```

Delete a Qdrant collection and reset chunk_count so it repopulates.

Dry-run by default — shows how many artifacts would be re-embedded.
Pass --write to delete the collection and reset chunk_count.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--collection`, `-c` | required | Qdrant collection to rebuild (e.g. core-code, core-specs). |
| `--write` | off | Apply the rebuild (default: dry-run). |

### `core vectors status` {#vectors-status}

```
core vectors status
```

Show vector store health and collection statistics.

### `core vectors sync` {#vectors-sync}

```
core vectors sync [OPTIONS]
```

Synchronize constitutional documents to vector collections.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` | off | Apply changes to Qdrant. |
| `--target`, `-t` | `all` | Target: policies, patterns, or all |

### `core vectors sync-code` {#vectors-sync-code}

```
core vectors sync-code [OPTIONS]
```

Synchronize codebase symbol embeddings with the vector database.

| Argument / option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` | off | Commit vectors to Qdrant. |
| `--force` | off | Force re-vectorization of all symbols. |
